argv: # The LIVE divergence register for the Rust port -- the AUTHORITATIVE
# list of inputs where rs/ produces a different RESULT from the canonical
# ts/. DIVERGENCE.md at the repository root explains the shape of each
# disagreement and points here; this file is what RUNS, so if the two ever
# disagree, this one wins.
# Six tab-separated columns. `ts`, `go` and `rust` are what each port
# ACTUALLY produces today: the FIRST printed line as a JSON string, the
# same vocabulary as the `stdout` column of test/spec/*.tsv, or
# ERROR:<code>. `stdin` is the piped text, `issue` the repair that closes
# the row.
# This file is NOT in test/spec/, deliberately. Everything in that
# directory is discovered and run by all three suites, and a register
# belongs to the port that records it: rs/tests/divergence_test.rs runs
# this one and asserts the `rust` column. A row that gets FIXED fails as
# loudly as one that regresses, and must then be deleted -- that is the
# whole point of an executable ledger over a prose list.
# Divergences a single printed value cannot express -- the exit code, the
# text on standard error, the help text, the debug trace -- are pinned by
# tests in rs/tests/divergence_test.rs instead, and described in
# DIVERGENCE.md. Adding a row here is an admission of parity debt, not a
# way to silence a failing test.
# Nesting past 127 containers. tabnas-jsonic (Rust) refuses it with the
# engine's `cancel` code, because the engine walks a value with the call
# stack to display, convert or drop it, and a few thousand levels ended
# the process. TypeScript and Go have no limit. Measured at depth 128,
# the first depth that differs: depth 127 agrees in all three. The limit
# lives in tabnas/jsonic, not in this repo, and this row closes when that
# crate's does.
